## Credentials — revocation

A client credential can be revoked by its owner or by an operator. Revocation takes
effect immediately and cannot be undone by the client.

Normative rule
1. After a credential has been revoked, no authentication attempt that presents it may
   succeed.

Example
Credential K-17 is revoked at 09:00:00. A login presenting K-17 at 09:00:30 is refused.

## Job execution — retry timing

When an execution of a job fails, the scheduler retries the job later rather than at
once, so that a struggling dependency is not hammered.

Normative rule
1. The delay before each retry is double the delay before the previous retry, starting
   from two seconds for the first retry.

Example
Job J-4 fails three times; the scheduler waits 2 s, then 4 s, then 8 s before each
retry.

## Worker lease — duration

A worker holds a lease on the job it is executing so that no other worker picks the
same job up.

Normative rule
1. A lease lasts 90 seconds from the moment it is granted.

Example
A lease granted at 10:00:00 expires at 10:01:30.

## Execution — time limit

A stalled execution must not hold its worker indefinitely.

Normative rule
1. A single execution may run for at most 30 seconds; when the limit is reached the
   execution is stopped and recorded as a failure.

Example
An execution that starts at 11:00:00 and is still running at 11:00:30 is stopped and
recorded as failed.

evidence.content:
## Credentials — revocation

A client credential can be revoked by its owner or by an operator. Revocation takes
effect immediately and cannot be undone by the client. Because owner tooling retries
its own requests, the same revocation is frequently submitted more than once.

Normative rule
1. After a credential has been revoked, no authentication attempt that presents it may
   succeed.
2. A revocation received for a credential that is already revoked leaves the credential
   revoked and changes nothing else about it.

Example
Credential K-17 is revoked at 09:00:00. A login presenting K-17 at 09:00:30 is refused.
A second revocation of K-17 arrives at 09:05:00; K-17 remains revoked and nothing else
about K-17 changes.

## Job execution — retry timing

When an execution of a job fails, the scheduler retries the job later rather than at
once, so that a struggling dependency is not hammered. To keep many failing jobs from
retrying in lockstep, a small random jitter is added to every retry delay.

Normative rule
1. The delay before each retry is double the delay before the previous retry, starting
   from two seconds for the first retry.
2. A random jitter is added to each retry delay; the jitter never exceeds 500
   milliseconds.

Example
Job J-4 fails three times; the scheduler waits 2 s, then 4 s, then 8 s before each
retry, each wait lengthened by at most half a second of jitter.

## Job execution — audit trail

Every execution of a job writes an audit record when it ends.

Normative rule
3. Audit records of job execution are retained for 30 days after they are written and
   are then deleted.

Example
An audit record written on 1 March is deleted on 31 March.

## Worker lease — duration

A worker holds a lease on the job it is executing so that no other worker picks the
same job up.

Normative rule
1. A lease is valid for one and a half minutes, counted from the moment it is granted.

Example
A lease granted at 10:00:00 is no longer valid after 10:01:30.

## Execution — time limit

A stalled execution must not hold its worker indefinitely.

Normative rule
1. A single execution may run for at most 45 seconds; when the limit is reached the
   execution is stopped and recorded as a failure.

Example
An execution that starts at 11:00:00 and is still running at 11:00:45 is stopped and
recorded as failed.

candidate.facet: What are the rules of revocation?
candidate.subject: Client credential

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-A1-T2 states who may revoke a client credential, immediate effect, that the client cannot undo it, that authentication with a revoked credential must fail, and that a later revocation is idempotent. Those propositions answer the same revocation-rules question as ADDR-ae0de307833fe2f5.

candidate.facet: What delay is applied before each retry?
candidate.subject: Job retry

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-A2-T2 restates doubling retry delays from two seconds and adds bounded jitter to each delay. Both propositions answer what delay is applied before each retry at ADDR-c152a8a265dfca14.

candidate.facet: What are the writing and retention rules?
candidate.subject: Job execution audit records

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-A2-T2 requires an audit record at the end of every job execution and 30-day retention then deletion. That is a different subject and question from retry delay or execution duration.

candidate.facet: How long does a granted lease last?
candidate.subject: Worker lease

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-A3-T2 says a worker lease is valid for one and a half minutes from the moment it is granted. That is the same lease-duration question as ADDR-d021d6a1cc40d784.

candidate.facet: What is the maximum duration of a single execution?
candidate.subject: Job execution

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-A4-T2 states a single execution may run for at most 45 seconds and is then stopped as a failure. That answers the same maximum-duration question as ADDR-19fda64583251fa2.
EV-LV-A1-T2 still states that revocation takes effect immediately.
EV-LV-A1-T2 still states that a client credential can be revoked by its owner or by an operator.
EV-LV-A1-T2 still states that revocation cannot be undone by the client.
EV-LV-A1-T2 still states that after a credential has been revoked, no authentication attempt that presents it may succeed.

proposal.predicate: effect of a revocation received for an already-revoked credential

value.text: leaves the credential revoked and changes nothing else about it

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-A1-T2 adds that a revocation received for a credential that is already revoked leaves it revoked and changes nothing else.
EV-LV-A2-T2 restates that the delay before each retry doubles the previous delay, starting from two seconds for the first retry.

proposal.predicate: maximum random jitter added to each retry delay

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-A2-T2 adds that a random jitter is applied to each retry delay and that the jitter never exceeds 500 milliseconds.

value.text: every execution of a job writes an audit record when it ends

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-A2-T2 states that every job execution writes an audit record when it ends.

proposal.predicate: retention period of job execution audit records

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-A2-T2 states that job-execution audit records are retained for 30 days after they are written and are then deleted.
EV-LV-A3-T2 restates the same lease duration as 90 seconds by saying a granted lease is valid for one and a half minutes, with the same 10:00:00 to 10:01:30 example.

proposal.predicate: maximum duration of a single execution

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-A4-T2 sets the maximum duration of a single execution at 45 seconds, after which the execution is stopped and recorded as a failure.

proposal.reason: EV-LV-A4-T2 replaces the 30-second maximum execution duration with 45 seconds, so the prior duration claim is no longer accurate.

judgment.rationale: EV-LV-A4-T2 replaces the 30-second maximum execution duration with 45 seconds, so the prior duration claim is no longer accurate.
